Handwriter, end to end

The video

1. Type anything

Notes for Thursday

The market by the canal opens at seven, so I will leave the house a little before six and walk the long way round past the old mill.

Things to bring: a jar for the honey, two cloth bags, exact change and the list Maya gave me. She wants 3 lemons, 12 eggs and a loaf of the dark rye bread.

A quick sum for the paving job. The yard is a square of side x, so its area is x^2. We only pave \frac{3}{4} of it, which leaves \frac{1}{4} for the herb bed. If x = 6 then 36 - 27 = 9 square metres stay green.

Remember to ring Jon about the ladder, pay the window cleaner, and ask whether the choir still meets on the first Friday of every month.

On the way back, stop at the library before it shuts at 5 and return the two books on bridges. The fine is 40 cents a day, so 3 days late costs 1.20 in total.

For the weekend: fix the gate latch, plant the beans in rows 30 cm apart, and write to Aunt Zelda to thank her for the quilt.

None of these sentences were in the pages the letters came from. Every word here is put together from single letters and joined pairs, then spaced, slanted and wobbled the way the measured habits say.

1148 characters, none of it from the pages the letters were traced from. x^2 and \frac{3}{4} are layout markup.

2. It is written in the handwriting

1855 pen strokes on a letter page, built from 154 letters and joined groups (364 samples) and the habits measured from real pages. Characters with no sample: none.

3. Stroke by stroke

The same strokes in the order the pen will make them.

4. It becomes a file for the Bambu Lab P1S

Part 1: 1055 strokes, about 21 min, 36653 lines of G-code, safety faults: 0. Part 2: 800 strokes, about 16 min, 27523 lines of G-code, safety faults: 0. With Falu's clearances the pen reaches 206 mm across and 199 mm front to back, so a letter page takes 2 passes.

5. Read back from the G-code

The picture is redrawn only from the printer commands. Furthest any point lands from where it was meant to: 0.07 mm. The pen goes down 1600 times for 1855 strokes, because strokes that meet are drawn without lifting.

6. The pencil holder

The pencil guide from this project in Falu's head mount with his D9 spring module. Overlap with the mount's clip rings: 1.36 mm³ (snug). Pencil against guide and spring: 0.0 and 0.0 mm³ (free).

What this demo does not show

Nothing here has run on a real printer: the files pass a simulated safety check only, the pen offsets are uncalibrated (0, 0) and the holder has not been printed.
